app.title: planetMagFields App: 3D field explorer and orbit trajectory field calculator
app.summary: A person picks a planet and one of its published magnetic field models, and sets the radial level, units and resolution. They read the radial field drawn on a rotatable 3D sphere with traced field lines, alongside header figures and, if they choose, the power spectrum by degree and the energy fractions. On a second page they bring in a trajectory of points by pasting, uploading or generating an orbit. The interface computes the field components at every point and shows them on a 3D track, as stacked line charts and as a table, and the person downloads the results as a CSV.

task.text: Explore a planet's published magnetic field model in 3D and compute the model field at the points of a spacecraft trajectory, to export as a table.

data.text: Published field models given as spherical harmonic (Gauss) coefficients, evaluated as a continuous field over a sphere and the space around it; trajectories are tables of points in spherical coordinates, which get field components added.
data.item: a planetary field model at a chosen radial level; on the trajectory page, one trajectory point (r, colatitude, longitude) with its computed field components

stage.text: exploring published field models and computing model field values along an orbit for later analysis

mechanism.text: A sidebar of controls (planet, model, year, radius, units, colour scale, field-line settings) redraws a rotatable 3D sphere coloured by radial field, with traced field lines and an optional power-spectrum panel beside it. On the trajectory page, tabs for pasting, uploading or generating points feed a computation whose results appear in tabs for a 3D track, stacked component charts and a table, with a CSV download.

field.text: spherical harmonic magnetic field models in planetary science

workflow.name: pick a reference model, inspect it, and sample it at given points to a file

steps.step: choose the reference model to work with
steps.here: Choose a planet and one of its models, which links to the model's paper. For Earth, a year slider sets the epoch. Radius, units and resolution can each be reset with a button.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: The radial field is drawn on a rotatable 3D sphere at the chosen radius. Field lines are traced outward to a maximum radius, Earth can show coastlines, and the colormap and limits can be set. Hovering reads Br at a point.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The header shows ℓmax, dipole tilt and radius. 'Show spectrum' adds the Lowes spectrum by degree on a log axis, with axial and total dipolarity and the axisymmetric and equatorially symmetric energy fractions.

Bring in trajectory points with columns r, theta and phi: paste them, upload a CSV, or generate an elliptical orbit from a point count, periapsis, apoapsis and inclination. Angle units are set to radians or degrees, and rows that are not valid numbers are dropped with a warning.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The model field (Br, Bθ, Bφ, |B|) is computed at every point. Tabs show the 3D track over the planet's surface field (coloured by the chosen component), three stacked line charts against point index, and the full table.
'Download results CSV' saves the input coordinates with the field components and magnitude added, in a file named after the planet and model.

distinctive: The field is extended away from the surface by potential-field extrapolation, so the radius slider shows it at depth or at altitude, and trajectory points off the surface get modelled values.
Field lines are integrated as ODEs from seed points chosen by field strength, split between strong positive and strong negative regions, so both open and closed lines appear.
Earth's model depends on time: its coefficients are interpolated to any epoch from 1900 to 2030.
The field is summarised by its spherical harmonic power spectrum (Lowes) with dipolarity and symmetry fractions, the usual way of comparing planetary dynamo fields.
Trajectories can be generated as test orbits from periapsis, apoapsis and inclination, as well as pasted or uploaded.
